system_boundary: The repository does not contain one unified general-purpose USG chatbot. It contains separate implementation lines, structured semantic services, versioned native models, adapters, and bounded text-interpreters. Each must be evaluated independently through its actual entry point.

capability_state_definitions.bounded_benchmark_enabled: A frozen benchmark supports the stated construction/task scope only; never generalize beyond that scope.
capability_state_definitions.implemented_regression_tested: Code and regression tests exist; this does not by itself establish semantic correctness.
capability_state_definitions.historical_baseline: A preserved versioned baseline; test it as its own runtime and do not silently substitute it for another version.
capability_state_definitions.model_only: A native record/model API, not a complete language parser or end-to-end interpretation pipeline.
capability_state_definitions.partial_candidate_only: Code or candidate evidence exists, but the relevant acceptance/gold-data gate is not complete.

components.name: JavaScript Semantic Workbench

entry_points.mode: Windows launcher; starts Node bridge when available, otherwise static local UI

capabilities.boundary: Model generation/repair and deterministic structural checks; semantic quality of a live model is not established by fake-server tests.
Finite English source-composition patterns; unsupported forms use the optional model-proposal path.
Preserves typed runtime failures and raw response evidence; same model reviews its own output.

limitations: Does not provide unrestricted English or multilingual understanding.
Deterministic tests use fixtures and a fake Ollama-compatible endpoint; they do not establish live Qwen/Gemma semantic accuracy.
Human review is required before propositions are accepted into the knowledge base.
components.evaluation_policy: Run the JavaScript workbench independently from Python services. Use local deterministic mode for reproducible smoke tests; tag model-assisted runs separately and record model/runtime configuration.

components.name: Python reference kernel snapshots

capabilities.boundary: Version-specific APIs, representations, and package-local tests; not the same runtime as the top-level Kernel Lab application.
v0.5.0 adds predicate application, connective, and quantifier constructors relative to v0.4.0.

limitations: The repository identifies v0.4.0 as the current archived baseline; v0.4.0 and v0.5.0 must remain separately versioned test targets.
Passing package tests does not establish unrestricted natural-language understanding.
Do not infer interoperability from co-location; use the explicit adapters.
components.evaluation_policy: Pin the exact kernel directory/version and its PYTHONPATH for every run. Do not combine its scores with the top-level local API or browser workbench.

components.name: Python native semantic-record model generations

entry_points.mode: Typed UnresolvedItem model API; v1.2.0 is historical

capabilities.boundary: Each version exposes its own typed model and package-local tests; these packages do not independently parse user language.

limitations: Native model validation is not end-to-end interpretation.
The model generations are independently versioned packages and are not one monolithic kernel.
The v1.2.1 typed UnresolvedItem generation supersedes the initial v1.2.0 model for composed adapter use.
components.evaluation_policy: Test constructors, invariants, equality/identity, and serialization independently. Never score these model-only APIs as language-understanding entry points.

components.name: Loss-preserving Python USG-SEM/1.0 document adapters
components.version: family adapters v0.5.0-v1.4.0; composed adapter v1.5.1

capabilities.boundary: Family-specific exact projections; unsupported fields remain in the canonical envelope and are reported.
v1.5.1 composes family adapters over one immutable snapshot and checks cross-family spans.

limitations: PARTIAL mapping is an explicit compatibility result, not proof that all canonical records are natively represented.
Unsupported constructors or metadata are rejected or preserved canonically rather than silently coerced.
components.evaluation_policy: Use canonical USG-SEM fixtures and adapter-specific mapping reports. Test import and export separately and verify the canonical envelope remains loss-preserving.

components.name: Phase 2 structured semantic-reasoning services

capabilities.boundary: Operates on registered structured semantic data, rules, evidence, and queries; does not interpret arbitrary natural-language user requests.

limitations: Deterministic rule execution and benchmark success do not establish general reasoning across arbitrary requests.
Only benchmark-supported structured tasks may receive semantic correctness scores.
components.evaluation_policy: Test structured reasoning APIs with registered inputs and explicit oracles. Keep this population distinct from raw-text interpreter trials.

components.name: Phase 3 canonical semantic graph store and persistent query service

capabilities.boundary: SQLite is the sole canonical persistence authority; immutable revisions, integrity checks, export, and replay are within scope.
DuckDB, LanceDB, Qdrant, and RocksDB/Rocksdict are comparison/evaluation paths, not replacements for SQLite authority.

limitations: Persistence and query correctness do not imply natural-language interpretation.
Alternative database experiments must not be treated as the live canonical store.
components.evaluation_policy: Use isolated temporary SQLite files per scenario; evaluate integrity, revision conflicts, retrieval, export, and replay without sharing mutable state across cases.

components.name: Phase 4 raw-text interpretation demonstrator

capabilities.boundary: Small bounded English/MSA Arabic demonstrator with source, lexical, syntax, composition, mention, discourse, assertion/evidence and resource stages.

limitations: Not a general-purpose English or Arabic parser.
The Phase 4 benchmark scope is a bounded offline demonstrator and is not broad language coverage.
components.evaluation_policy: Invoke the Phase 4 service/endpoint separately and measure completion status, source spans, schema validity, and unsupported/ambiguous outcomes.

components.name: Phase 5 multi-stage interpretation pipeline

capabilities.boundary: Lexical, segmentation, syntax, operator, semantic-composition, and discourse artifacts with versioned resource catalogue and immutable run replay.

limitations: The Phase 5 v0.2 pipeline does not emit a USG-SEM/1.0 document.
The accepted 100-fixture benchmark measures three simple-transitive English/MSA Arabic target constructions; it does not establish broad language coverage.
Discourse/association candidates do not resolve identity or objective truth.
components.evaluation_policy: Record the Phase 5 result envelope and resource manifest digest. Do not score it as canonical USG-SEM output or as unrestricted language understanding.

components.name: Phase 6 extended construction and nominal-candidate work

capabilities.boundary: Phase 6 Steps 6.1-6.5 are accepted only for their frozen, bounded English/MSA Arabic scopes.
Step 6.6 remains blocked: external parser/PUD audits and candidate corpora are not an independent bilingual semantic-gold acceptance set.

limitations: The current Phase 6 roadmap states Step 6.6 remains in progress and Step 6.7 remains blocked.
External parser baselines are structural proxies, not human-adjudicated semantic-role/modifier gold.
Candidate code and a passing candidate benchmark do not promote the capability to accepted.
components.evaluation_policy: Evaluate accepted 6.1-6.5 profiles separately from 6.6 candidates. Never treat an external parser baseline as USG semantic gold.

components.name: USG Kernel Lab, local HTTP API, and command-line interface

capabilities.boundary: USG-SEM/1.0 schema validation, SQLite document/revision API, query, integrity, export.

capabilities.area: Phase 4 and Phase 5 text entry points
capabilities.boundary: Exposes versioned, bounded interpreters; does not unify every model package or JS workbench into one runtime.

limitations: Local API and Kernel Lab bind to loopback, not a public multi-user service.
Phase 5 and Phase 4 results have different contracts and capabilities.
The README explicitly states GET /v1/health is not defined; GET /health is the health endpoint.
components.evaluation_policy: Test HTTP, CLI, and browser adapters as distinct interfaces over their shared dispatcher. Use a fresh temporary database per case.

components.name: JavaScript Workbench to USG-SEM/1.0 adapter

entry_points.mode: Workbench semantic model to canonical USG-SEM/1.0 adapter

capabilities.boundary: Converts Workbench semantic core representation with mapping/validation reports; not a parser.

limitations: Partial mapping is expected where the target model lacks an exact representation.
Source offsets and canonical-only records must be explicitly preserved.
components.evaluation_policy: Evaluate as a serialization/conformance boundary, not as a natural-language understanding entry point.

contracts.role: canonical semantic interchange and preservation envelope
Versioned native model and document-adapter contracts

known_gaps: No open-world randomized scenario generator is present yet.
No unified isolated execution runner covers every implementation/interface.
No common evaluation-result schema or append-only report store is present yet.
No repository-owned, independently licensed naturalistic request corpus has been imported for this program.
No adaptive discovery loop currently promotes novel failure clusters into reviewable regression fixtures.
The repository has distinct runtimes and bounded capabilities; no single executable exposes every USG model, interpreter, and adapter as one unified system.
inventory_conclusions: The test subject must be selected by implementation and version, not by the generic label 'USG'.
A model-only API, adapter, structured reasoning service, text interpreter, and browser workbench are different evaluation targets.
Only benchmark-enabled capability scopes may receive semantic correctness scores.
Unsupported, partial, unknown, ambiguous, and infrastructure-error outcomes must remain distinct.
